t: LeetCode 2217 - Find Palindrome With Fixed Length: Build the Half, Mirror the Rest
o: **Understanding the problem.** For several ranks k we must return the k-th smallest palindrome with exactly intLength digits, or -1 if fewer than k exist. A palindrome of length L is completely determined by its first ceil(L/2) digits, called the half: the remaining digits are a mirror image, with odd lengths sharing the middle digit. Ordering palindromes numerically is the same as ordering their halves, and valid halves run over all ceil(L/2)-digit numbers from 10^(ceil(L/2)-1) (no leading zero) to 10^(ceil(L/2)) - 1, giving exactly 9 * 10^(ceil(L/2)-1) palindromes. Hence the k-th palindrome is the mirror of 10^(ceil(L/2)-1) + k - 1. In Example 1 (L = 3) halves 10..99 produce 101..999, so query 90 maps to half 99 -> 999. In Example 2 (L = 4) half 15 -> "15" + "51" = 1551 for query 6.
k: Palindromes of length L biject with their first-half numbers, preserving numeric order.
There are exactly 9 * 10^(ceil(L/2)-1) of them; any larger rank returns -1.
Construction is direct: half = 10^(h-1) + k - 1, then append the reverse of half's first L - h digits.

a.i: Generate every integer of the requested length, keep those whose decimal form reverses to itself, and index into the collected list. This mirrors the definition perfectly and is fine for toy lengths, but the count grows tenfold per extra digit, so it collapses long before the constraint ceiling of 15 digits.
s: Set lo = 10^(L-1) and hi = 10^L as the length range.
Collect every x in [lo, hi) whose string equals its reverse.
Answer each query as the (k-1)-th entry, or -1 when k exceeds the list size.
a.t: O(10^L * L) - tests every L-digit integer with an O(L) palindrome check
a.sp: O(P * L) - stores all P palindromes of the length

a.i: Skip enumeration entirely: compute h = ceil(L/2), reject ranks above 9 * 10^(h-1), turn the rank into the half value 10^(h-1) + k - 1, and mirror it by appending the reverse of its first L - h characters. Odd lengths reuse the middle digit automatically because L - h = h - 1 there. Each query costs one small addition plus an O(L) string splice.
s: For each query k > capacity, output -1.
Append reverse(half.substring(0, intLength - halfLen)) and output the number.
a.t: O(Q * L) - each of Q queries performs an O(L) construction
a.sp: O(L) - scratch string per query besides the output

w: Go straight to half-construction once you notice the bijection; the brute force exists mostly to sanity-check examples. Pitfalls: leading zeros force the half to start at 10^(h-1); the mirrored slice is intLength - halfLen characters, which correctly shares the middle digit for odd lengths; results reach 10^15, so C++/Java must use 64-bit types while JavaScript Numbers stay safe below 2^53. Watch that -1 answers are returned in position, not compressed. Follow-ups: count palindromes in [lo, hi] for fixed length, or support 'next palindrome greater than x' queries with the same half trick.
